images.title: Two diameters and the shape they make
images.purpose: Show a circle of diameter 10 cm with two diameters whose four ends are joined to make a rectangle, and the same circle with the two diameters at right angles, which makes a square.
images.composition: Two equal circles side by side. The left one has two slanted diameters and a rectangle; the right one has two diameters at right angles and a square. Names and sizes sit under the circles.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, two circles of the same size side by side with a heading at the top left. Scale: 40 px for each 1 cm, so a circle of diameter 10 cm is 400 px across. HEADING: the text Two diameters, four ends joined in bold dark #1F2937 sans-serif (44 px), left edge at x 80, about y 70. LEFT CIRCLE: centre (370, 400), radius 200 px (diameter 400 px), thin dark #2B2B2B outline (4 px), white inside. Two diameters, each a straight teal #0072B2 line (5 px) through the centre: diameter 1 horizontal from (170, 400) to (570, 400); diameter 2 slanted from (241, 553) to (499, 247). Four teal end dots (18 px) at (570, 400), (499, 247), (170, 400), (241, 553). The four ends are joined in that order and back to the first by 4 straight dark #2B2B2B sides (6 px) that make a rectangle with sides about 169 px and 363 px, filled amber #E69F00 at 40 percent opacity (the diameters stay visible on top). A reddish purple #CC79A7 dot (16 px) on the centre (370, 400) with the label centre (30 px) at (418, 432). Four small white square right angle marks (22 px, thin dark outline), one inside each corner of the rectangle, their sides lying along the two sides of that corner. Under the circle: the word rectangle in bold dark text (56 px) centred at (370, 660), and under it the text diameter 10 cm, radius 5 cm (34 px) centred at (370, 720). RIGHT CIRCLE: centre (1086, 400), radius 200 px, same outline. Two teal diameters at right angles: horizontal from (886, 400) to (1286, 400) and vertical from (1086, 200) to (1086, 600). Four teal end dots (18 px) at the four ends. The four ends are joined in order by 4 straight dark sides (6 px) that make a square with sides of about 283 px, filled green #009E73 at 40 percent opacity. A reddish purple dot (16 px) on the centre (1086, 400). Four small white square right angle marks (22 px) one inside each corner of the square. Under the circle: the word square in bold dark text (56 px) centred at (1086, 660), and under it the text a special rectangle (34 px) centred at (1086, 720). In all: 2 circles, 4 diameters, 8 end dots, 2 centre dots, 2 four-sided shapes and 8 right angle marks. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of circles, diameters, dots or right angle marks that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
a diameter that does not pass through the centre
a four-sided shape that is not a rectangle, or a square on the left circle
images.takeaway: Joining the four ends of two diameters always makes a rectangle with four right angles; when the diameters cross at a right angle the rectangle is a square.
images.description: A circle of diameter 10 cm with two diameters joined into a rectangle, and a second circle with two diameters at right angles joined into a square, each with right angle marks.
images.context: Concept image for Two Diameters Make a Rectangle. It shows the concept's own circle of diameter 10 cm and not a figure from your maths book.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the centre first: both diameters pass through it, so the four ends are all the same distance from it. The slip to watch is expecting a kite or any other four-sided shape.

image_decisions.why: The two diameters, their four joined ends and the right angle marks are the mathematics: the child sees the equal opposite sides and the four right angles in the picture.
